body: It seems that the default behavior is kinda weird, forcing the normal happy path usage to implement two hooks or you get nonsensical error messages for even 404 pages. Why are those hooks not simply the default, and people can override it if needed?

Because your message could contain sensitive data like "an error occurred using \<secret api key\>". Also, it's not ensured that the `error` passed in is actually an `Error` object - anything can be thrown.

I get all that, but even without any custom code at all, just creating a new project and hitting a 404, you get a pretty bad error message. That is the default behavior right now, and you have to work to fix that default behavior. I would hope the default would be better. Working with SvelteKit keeps getting a tiny bit more complex bit by bit. It's a great framework, don't get me wrong, but recent changes are not all for the better when it comes to DX (and UX) I think.

How would a better default look like that
- shows a 404 message in case of a 404
- doesn't show any message that any error has because it could contain sensitive data
- is consistent and concise to explain?

?

> doesn't show any message that any error has because it could contain sensitive data

I think the default behavior shouldn't maybe be concerned with that, and leave it to developers to add logic on top of the default logic if they want to filter out stuff. But by default just show the message property in the error as-is. That would show a 404 message in case of a 404, show all other error messages, and is consistent and concise to explain. You only have to explain how to alter the default behavior, same as now. But the default would be better, in most cases most developers won't ever have to change the default, whereas now you kinda always have to override it because the default behavior is bad.

body:
A way to avoid `handleError` for this altogether would be to create a catch-all fallback route for this, which you can design however you like: ```html // src/routes/[...notfound]/+page.svelte

Not found

etc etc

```

Reopening this — we shouldn't be calling `handleError` in the case of a 404. In this case it's coming from here: https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/blob/d2db7edff6a969ea79c1a1ba6576b489d38ed92d/packages/kit/src/runtime/server/page/respond_with_error.js#L82
Should we make 404 page with some default message with the possibility to opt out and handle the error using `handleError`?

When implementing this, one problem is that `App.PageError` could contain more than `{ message: string }` so any access to `$page.error`, for example in `+error.svelte` could expect more properties to be available. This makes it hard for these 404s to _not_ go through `handleError`, just returning `{ message: 'Not found' }` wouldn't be enough here.

If we were to keep calling `handleError` in the 404 case we could make it so that the error is a `Error404` defined by SvelteKit which both the fallback (`{ message: error instanceof Error404 ? 'Not Found' : 'Internal Error' }` and the user could check for.

@Rich-Harris Sorry, I'm a bit confused. Are you saying 404s should be handled with `handleError` (your last message seems to suggest that) or are you saying they shouldn't (your first message seems to suggest that)?

Thanks 🙏

issue.title: GET in +server.ts gets called twice
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

The method GET gets called twice. Following is a sample code:

```
let counter = 0;

export const GET = async () => {
  counter++;
  return new Response(`count: ${counter}`);
};
```

The responses on consecutive page visits on browser are:
```
count: 1
count: 3
count: 5
count: 7
```

Interestingly the same is not the case, when I call the APIs using Postman, fetch (which give the correct output i.e., GET gets called only once).

### Reproduction

Reproduce by creating a file route/+server.ts with the following contents:
```
let counter = 0;

export const GET = async () => {
  counter++;
  return new Response(`count: ${counter}`);
};
```
Visit localhost:5173/ on browser.

### Logs

_No response_

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 12.5.1
    CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz
    Memory: 20.55 MB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 3.2.57 - /bin/bash
  Binaries:
    Node: 16.17.0 - /usr/local/bin/node
    npm: 8.15.0 - /usr/local/bin/npm
  Browsers:
    Brave Browser: 105.1.43.89
    Chrome: 105.0.5195.102
    Firefox: 104.0.2
    Safari: 15.6.1
  npmPackages:
    @sveltejs/adapter-auto: next => 1.0.0-next.72 
    @sveltejs/kit: next => 1.0.0-next.480 
    svelte: ^3.44.0 => 3.50.1 
    vite: ^3.1.0 => 3.1.0
```


### Severity

serious, but I can work around it

### Additional Information

The GET method needs to be called only once.

body: @Rich-Harris Do you think it makes sense to return `App.PageError` from the server side `handleError` function, to allow to return another HTTP status code than 500? I see the `handleError` as a global error handler for all the server side code. If I throw a specific error in my API that some thing could not be found, I would like that the error handler catches the error, logs it and then still returns 404 to the client. Currently I think this is not possible. I could create an issue if you think this makes sense.
